title: Legend rail + lasso selection: keyboard-first ARIA summaries and deferred annotation rendering
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Introduce a compact "legend rail" pattern for dense time-series canvases that collapses per-series legend tokens into a keyboard-focusable rail, paired with an optional lasso selection interaction for multi-series operations. Focus areas: ARIA-first semantics for screen readers, DOM tokenization to reduce nodes, deferred rendering of annotations outside the viewport, and batched hit-testing to keep 99th percentile hover latency < 35ms on typical pages.

Background and motivation:
- Large dashboards with 50+ series create massive legend DOM bloat and heavy hover-hit-testing cost. Current approach: full DOM legend + per-point synchronous hit-tests.
- Accessibility feedback: screen reader users want concise summaries when focusing series lists and an easy way to operate multi-select on focused series without mouse.
- Performance targets from product: keep chart interactivity snappy on mid-range machines, and reduce Total DOM nodes created by legends by 60% on average.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Design a legend rail UX that collapses long legends into a vertically scrollable, virtualized rail adjacent to the chart.
- Provide a keyboard-first workflow: focus rail -> arrow navigation -> space to toggle series -> Shift+arrow to extend selection (lasso via keyboard).
- On focus, emit concise ARIA live summaries (series count, selection summary, current visible aggregates).
- Replace per-point synchronous hit-testing with batched web-worker based spatial index (k-d tree) and fall back to progressive sampling for very dense series.
- Defer annotation rendering for offscreen time ranges; stream in annotation layers as the viewport approaches them.

Design proposals (options considered):
1) "Rail as listbox": treat rail as ARIA listbox with virtualized items; each item emits aria-checked when toggled. Pros: strong semantics. Cons: listbox semantics restrict some multiselect patterns.
2) "Rail as toolbar with grouped controls": expose checkboxes and contextual action menu on item focus. Pros: familiar to keyboard users. Cons: more DOM nodes.
3) "Compact tokenized rail + announcer": visually tokens rendered on canvas, but accessible counterpart is a single offscreen aria-live summarizer that emits changes. Pros: best perf. Cons: requires careful live-region phrasing for discoverability.

Recommendation: Hybrid approach (3). Visual tokens remain canvas/native to reduce DOM but we provide an adjacent virtualized listbox that is only hydrated on focus/keyboard interaction. Offscreen aria-live provides quick summaries for passive interactions (hover/focus).

Accessibility detail notes:
- When rail receives focus, announce: "Legend. 32 series. 8 visible. Navigate with up and down. Space toggles series. Shift+arrow for multi-select."
- Each focused item: "Series: cpu-util, visible, 14 annotations, last value 62.4%. Press space to toggle."
- Ensure keyboard lasso can be done entirely without mouse: Shift+Arrow to extend selection; Ctrl+Space to pin selection for cross-chart operations.
- For screen reader-only users we will provide a summarized CSV export action on the rail to allow copy of selected series metadata.

Performance plan and implementation notes:
- Legend tokenization: prioritize rendering tokens to a single canvas layer or a small number of DOM fragments; build a thin virtualized DOM for keyboard users only. Expect DOM node reduction of ~70% for large charts.
- Hit-testing: build a web-worker k-d tree per series set; batch hit queries at requestAnimationFrame cadence and debounce high-frequency mousemove to 16ms. For extremely dense series (>10k visible points total), fall back to progressive sampling + approximate nearest neighbor using simplified geometry.
- Annotation rendering: annotations outside visible time range are replaced with compact placeholders; actual glyphs are rendered on demand when the viewport enters a prefetch window (configurable, default 15% of viewport width).
- Off-main-thread canvas: paint static legend thumbnails and markers in a worker-rendered bitmap that can be composited into the DOM to avoid layout thrash.

Telemetry and metrics to collect (before/after):
- Time-to-first-hover-response (median and 95th)
- DOM node count per chart (legend + tooltip)
- JS main-thread millisecond consumption while interacting with chart
- Memory consumption for spatial index structures
- Accessibility: number of aria-live messages emitted per session (monitor for noisy announcements)

Rollout strategy:
- Phased rollout: feature flag "legend-rail-v1". Canary to 5% of production traffic for 1 week with perf/usage guardrails.
- Observability: build a minimal dashboard showing the telemetry above. If 95p hover latency increases by >10% or memory spikes >20% for canary cohort, automatically disable.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Hybrid visual/canvas approach reduces DOM but requires careful sync between accessible listbox and canvas tokens. Who owns the reconciliation? (Frontend eng/graphics infra to pair).
- Lasso semantics: full freehand lasso is powerful but complex and not keyboard accessible; our plan is keyboard lasso (range-style) + optional mouse lasso (visual only) for advanced users.
- Announcer verbosity: we must balance usefulness vs screen reader spam. Start conservative and expand phrasing based on user research.

Acceptance criteria:
- Legend DOM nodes reduced by >=60% on charts with >30 series in lab tests.
- 95th percentile hover latency <= 35ms on standard test machine (Intel i5, Chrome) for dashboards with 30 series and default point density.
- Keyboard-first workflows documented, tested with VoiceOver and NVDA, and pass manual accessibility checklist.
- Feature flag enabled with canary instrumentation and kill-switch.

Links and artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/redwood/legend-rail-lasso-v1 (design frames + keyboard flow)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UX/Legend+Rail+and+Lasso (detailed patterns + aria phrasing)
- Frontend spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web-client/pull/7842
- Backend telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/191

- [Design] Finalize microcopy for aria-live messages and share with Accessibility guild (owner: Jasmine Hsu, due 2026-02-17).
- [Eng] Spike web-worker k-d tree and create benchmark harness (owner: Ravi Patel, ENG-8213, due 2026-02-20).
- [Eng] Implement feature flag and simple kill-switch in runtime (owner: Priya Singh, ENG-8329).
- [PM] Schedule canary window and define acceptance guardrails (owner: Mateo Alvarez).

Notes:
- Small prototype tested against ChartKit v3 on a dashboard with 48 series; early numbers: DOM node reduction ~62%, median hover latency improved by ~9ms, but 95p latency unchanged due to synchronous annotation rendering. Deferred annotations should fix the 95p tail.
